body.statement: For every \(\mathfrak G\in\mathfrak E\), the value \(M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\) is attained by a globally honest randomized rule and equals the supremum of the Lagrange dual over finite nonnegative atomic coverage measures on the regions \(D_v\) and finite atomic probability measures on \(H_r\). Every finite atomic dual is a valid lower certificate, and an increasing enumeration of rational atoms converges upward to \(M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\) without a bounded-support premise.
body.justification: Attainment and dense atomic duality identify the exact object that the outward primal and dual programs must enclose.
body.gap: Goldenshluger, Juditsky, and Nemirovski establish compact-convex pairwise detector saddles, and Schafer and Stark approximate compact-parameter minimax expected size; neither treats globally honest finite-label rules over an unbounded fan.
body.consumer: CertGluePFL obtains valid lower endpoints without assuming that least-favorable mass is spatially tight.
